uncited: Parallelism and Distribution refers to the family of techniques that map volume rendering computations across multiple processing units (CPUs, GPUs, or networked nodes) to handle datasets or frame rates that exceed single-device capabilities.
It solves the scalability bottleneck of rendering large, high-resolution, or time-varying volumes by partitioning the workload spatially, temporally, or algorithmically.

It sets itself apart from sibling methods like [Tiled Parallel Compositing](1192-tiled-parallel-compositing.md) (which focuses on intra-node tile management) and [Compute Shader Kernel](1202-compute-shader-kernel.md) (which focuses on single-device kernel structure) by addressing inter-node communication, load balancing across heterogeneous clusters, and distributed memory management.
**Step:** Initialize distributed process group with NCCL backend: `dist.init_process_group("nccl", rank=rank, world_size=world_size)`.
Wrap model in DDP: `model = DDP(model.to(rank), device_ids=[rank])`.
Use `DistributedSampler` for data loading to ensure each GPU processes unique data.
**Parameter:** Master address is `localhost` and port is `12355`.
Parallel volume rendering has evolved from early distributed ray casting on clusters to modern GPU-based tiled and hybrid approaches.
